```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
# run from the repo root (the folder holding renv.lock) so the relative paths
# in r/paths.R resolve whether the qmd is rendered or run chunk by chunk
root <- getwd()
while (!file.exists(file.path(root, "renv.lock")) && dirname(root) != root) root <- dirname(root)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = root)
```

## Objective

Pull gridded vessel presence (VP) and apparent fishing effort (AFE) from the
GFW 4Wings API for the Ørsted projects AOI, 2016 onward, and write the raw
extracts to `data/raw/gfw/`. Nothing is filtered here: vessel classification
is done by `03_review_vessels.qmd` and `04_classify_aggregate.qmd`.

GFW reprocesses its data and relabels vessels between pipeline versions, so a
new pull will not reproduce the 2026-10-06 one (pipeline v4). Each pull is
filed under its version, `data/raw/gfw/<pipeline>/`, and this file **refuses
to overwrite** extracts already in that folder.

gfwr's own pull functions always request a dataset's `:latest` version, which
moves when GFW releases a new pipeline. So this file pulls through
`gfw_4wings_pinned()` (`r/gfw_helpers.R`), which sends the same request with
the dataset version named, and records the dataset IDs in `pull_info.csv`.
The 2026-10-06 pull predates it and was made at `:latest`, which was then v4.

It is left out of the project render list in `r/_quarto.yml`. Render it on its
own, only when a new pull is intended, naming the folder and the version:

```sh
quarto render r/01_pull_gfw.qmd -P pipeline:v5 -P dataset_version:v5.0
```

## Libraries

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)

# shared paths, and the pinned 4Wings pull (gfw_4wings_pinned())
source("r/paths.R")
source("r/gfw_helpers.R")

# Both must be named: a default folder would file a pull under whatever
# version this repo last analysed, and a default dataset version would pull
# whatever GFW serves now. Run chunk by chunk, set
# `params <- list(pipeline = "v5", dataset_version = "v5.0")`.
named <- \(p) exists("params") && !is.null(params[[p]]) && !identical(params[[p]], "")
stopifnot(
  "set the version folder: -P pipeline:v5" = named("pipeline"),
  "set the GFW dataset version: -P dataset_version:v5.0" = named("dataset_version"))
paths <- gfw_paths_with(params)

# the exact dataset IDs requested (gfw_dataset_id() refuses ":latest")
datasets <- c(vp  = gfw_dataset_id("presence", params$dataset_version),
              afe = gfw_dataset_id("fishing-effort", params$dataset_version))
message("Pulling ", paste(datasets, collapse = " and "),
        "; filing under pipeline ", paths$pipeline, ": ", paths$raw_gfw)

# never replace a pull: every later step and decision was made against it
existing <- Filter(file.exists, c(paths$raw_vp, paths$raw_afe, paths$pull_info))
if (length(existing) > 0) {
  stop("A pull is already filed under ", paths$pipeline, ": ",
       paste(existing, collapse = ", "),
       ". Use a new pipeline folder name, or move these files first.", call. = FALSE)
}
```

## Query window and spatial extent

```{r}
# the pull reads the token from GFW_TOKEN (project .Renviron; see r/00_setup.R)
stopifnot("GFW_TOKEN is not set; see r/00_setup.R" = Sys.getenv("GFW_TOKEN") != "")

# start included, end excluded (the pull of 2026-10-06 ran to 2026-09-30). The
# analysis window in r/gfw_helpers.R may end earlier; later steps drop the rest
query_start <- as.Date("2016-01-01")
query_end   <- as.Date("2026-10-01")

# The API takes at most 366 days per request, so the query runs one calendar
# year at a time. If a request still times out, split it into smaller ranges.
year_starts <- seq(query_start, query_end - 1, by = "year")
year_ends   <- pmin(year_starts + years(1), query_end)

tibble(start = year_starts, end = year_ends)
```

```{r}
# sf object passed to the `region` argument
orsted_aoi <- st_read(paths$aoi) |>
  select(geometry)

# map the AOI to make sure it was read correctly
ggplot(orsted_aoi) + geom_sf()
```

## Pull by year

Both datasets use the same arguments as the 2026-10-06 pull: 0.01° cells
(`HIGH`, about 1 km), daily, grouped by Vessel ID, over the AOI polygon. A
Vessel ID belongs to a single MMSI for a period of time, so one vessel can
have several IDs over time. No filter is applied, so GFW does no server-side
filtering by flag, gear or vessel type. Every column is read as text, so the
raw values are written back exactly as GFW sent them.

```{r}
pull_by_year <- function(dataset, label) {
  map2(year_starts, year_ends, \(s, e) {
    d <- gfw_4wings_pinned(dataset,
                           start_date          = format(s),
                           end_date            = format(e),
                           region              = orsted_aoi,
                           spatial_resolution  = "HIGH",
                           temporal_resolution = "DAILY",
                           group_by            = "VESSEL_ID")
    message(label, " ", format(s), " to ", format(e - 1), ": ", nrow(d), " records")
    d
  }) |>
    list_rbind()
}

gfw_vp_id  <- pull_by_year(datasets[["vp"]],  "VP")
gfw_afe_id <- pull_by_year(datasets[["afe"]], "AFE")
```

## Data summary

```{r}
summary(gfw_vp_id)
summary(gfw_afe_id)

count(gfw_vp_id, `Vessel Type`, sort = TRUE)
count(gfw_afe_id, `Vessel Type`, sort = TRUE)
```

```{r}
# records per month, by vessel type
bind_rows(VP = gfw_vp_id, AFE = gfw_afe_id, .id = "dataset") |>
  mutate(`Year Month` = floor_date(as.Date(`Time Range`), "month")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = `Year Month`, fill = `Vessel Type` == "FISHING")) +
  geom_bar() +
  facet_wrap(~ dataset, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(fill = "GFW FISHING") +
  theme_bw()
```

## Export the raw extracts

```{r}
dir.create(paths$raw_gfw, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

write_csv(gfw_vp_id,  paths$raw_vp)
write_csv(gfw_afe_id, paths$raw_afe)

# record when and how this pull was made; 03 and 04 read pull_date from it
write_csv(tibble(pull_date    = Sys.Date(),
                 pipeline     = paths$pipeline, # the version folder it is filed under
                 query_start  = query_start,
                 query_end    = query_end,
                 vp_rows      = nrow(gfw_vp_id),
                 afe_rows     = nrow(gfw_afe_id),
                 vp_dataset   = datasets[["vp"]],  # exact dataset IDs requested
                 afe_dataset  = datasets[["afe"]],
                 gfwr_version = as.character(packageVersion("gfwr")), # request mirrors this gfwr
                 api_base     = gfw_api_base),
          paths$pull_info)
```
